title: Claude models on Google Cloud, Anthropic-managed, are now generally available
summary: Anthropic-managed Claude models on Google Cloud are now generally available with full Claude Platform features, including Managed Agents (beta), code execution, computer use, skills, web search, MCP connector, caching, and batch, with new features shipping the same day as the native platform. Billing runs through a single Google Cloud invoice under Google Cloud IAM and counts toward existing commitments, with US and Global endpoints available. Fast Mode for Claude Opus 5.5 is also GA, offering up to 2.5x faster output at $8/$40 per million tokens, and a Google-managed option remains for data residency.

title: Agent observability on the Claude Platform
summary: Agent observability is in public beta on the Claude Platform, exporting OpenTelemetry traces from Managed Agents, the Messages API, and SDKs. Teams add a destination in Claude Console and get turns, model calls, and tool uses with latency, tokens, and IDs, following OTel GenAI semantic conventions and working with Grafana Cloud, Datadog, Honeycomb, and Langfuse. This helps verify agent reliability, debug issues, build evals, and track token usage.

title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop
summary: This guidance recommends replacing multi-agent orchestrator/subagent setups with a single agent loop, where domain knowledge lives in on-demand skills and tools load via tool search, and includes a migration kit. Single agents with skills often beat subagent designs on quality, cost, and latency, with one customer seeing about 2x faster runtime, and newer models can drop compensating harness logic. Teams should build a small eval and fold in one subagent at a time, keeping subagents for parallel work or context bloat.

title: How the Claude Code team does code review
summary: Claude writes about 90% of the Claude Code codebase, and its review is layered and mostly automated, with continuous review from pre-PR, multi-agent bug hunting with voting, security review that can block merges, and risk-based human approval. From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled and reverts fell over 40%, while PRs needing 5+ review rounds dropped from 8.9% to 1.5%. The post offers a checklist covering CLAUDE.md and REVIEW.md, risk tiers, and CODEOWNERS.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
summary: Anthropic built Scion, an in-house server-centric source control system that replaces git for its very large monorepo, completing the migration in about five months. It uses changesets instead of commits and sparse or virtual checkouts, cutting CPU and memory roughly 200x versus old git mirrors and reducing CI checkouts from minutes to seconds. Daily merged changes grew from about 2,500 in May 2026 to over 30,000 in September, driven by agents, and the system is not a general git replacement.

title: Code Review is now generally available
summary: Claude Code's automated PR review is now generally available for Team and Enterprise plans. Reviews finish in about 6-10 minutes, down from about 20 in preview, and findings are shorter and clearer, each stating the problem, trigger, and fix. Admins can set per-repo review depth (Quick, Standard by default, or Deep), and setup means enabling it in Claude Code settings, installing the GitHub App, and selecting repos.
